papers.title: Consistent Accelerated Inference via Confident Adaptive Transformers
papers.abstract: We develop a novel approach for confidently accelerating inference in the large and expensive multilayer Transformers that are now ubiquitous in natural language processing (NLP). Amortized or approximate computational methods increase efficiency, but can come with unpredictable performance costs. In this work, we present CATs -- Confident Adaptive Transformers -- in which we simultaneously increase computational efficiency, while guaranteeing a specifiable degree of consistency with the original model with high confidence. Our method trains additional prediction heads on top of intermediate layers, and dynamically decides when to stop allocating computational effort to each input using a meta consistency classifier. To calibrate our early prediction stopping rule, we formulate a unique extension of conformal prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on four classification and regression tasks.

summary_en.motivation: To accelerate inference in large Transformer models while maintaining consistency with the original model.
summary_en.method: Additional prediction heads on intermediate layers with a meta consistency classifier that decides early exit using conformal prediction calibration.
summary_en.result: Demonstrated speedups with guaranteed consistency on classification and regression tasks.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on four NLP benchmark datasets.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a copper-bearing titanium alloy for biomedical implants and investigate its processability via selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: The TC4-5Cu alloy was fabricated by SLM, followed by microstructural characterization, electrochemical tests, and wear-corrosion experiments.
summary_en.result: The TC4-5Cu alloy exhibits improved wear-corrosion resistance compared to standard TC4 alloy.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through electrochemical and wear-corrosion testing.

papers.title: Osseointegration of porous titanium and tantalum implants in ovariectomized rabbits: A biomechanical study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Today, biological fixation of uncemented press-fit acetabular components plays an important role in total hip arthroplasty. Long-term stable fixation of these implants depends on the osseointegration of the acetabular cup bone tissue into the acetabular cup implant, and their ability to withstand functional loads. AIM: To compare the strength of bone-implant osseointegration of four types of porous metal implants in normal and osteoporotic bone in rabbits. METHODS: The study was performed in 50 female California rabbits divided into non-ovariectomized (non-OVX) and ovariectomized groups (OVX) at 6 mo of age. Rabbits were sacrificed 8 wk after the implantation of four biomaterials [TTM, CONCELOC, Zimmer Biomet's Trabecular Metal (TANTALUM), and ATLANT] in a 5-mm diameter defect created in the left femur. A biomechanical evaluation of the femur was carried out by testing implant breakout force. The force was gradually increased until complete detachment of the implant from the bone occurred. RESULTS: The breakout force needed for implant detachment was significantly higher in the non-OVX group, compared with the OVX group for all implants (TANTALUM, 194.7 ± 6.1 N vs 181.3 ± 2.8 N; P = 0.005; CONCELOC, 190.8 ± 3.6 N vs 180.9 ± 6.6 N; P = 0.019; TTM, 186.3 ± 1.8 N vs 172.0 N ± 11.0 N; P = 0.043; and ATLANT, 104.9 ± 7.0 N vs 78.9 N ± 4.5 N; P = 0.001). In the OVX group, The breakout forces in TANTALUM, TTM, and CONCELOC did not differ significantly (P = 0.066). The breakout force for ATLANT in the OVX group was lower by a factor of 2.3 compared with TANTALUM and CONCELOC, and by 2.2 compared with TTM (P = 0.001). In the non-OVX group, the breakout force for ATLANT was significantly different from all other implants, with a reduction in fixation strength by a factor of 1.9 (P = 0.001). CONCLUSION: TANTALUM, TTM, and CONCELOC had equal bone-implant osseointegration in healthy and in osteoporotic bone. ATLANT had significantly decreased osseointegration (P = 0.001) in healthy and in osteoporotic bone.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较多孔金属植入物在正常和骨质疏松兔骨中的骨整合强度。
summary_zh.method: 在兔股骨植入4种多孔金属，8周后测量拔出强度。
summary_zh.result: TANTALUM、TTM、CONCELOC骨整合强度相当，ATLANT显著较弱。
summary_zh.validation: 动物体内实验验证骨整合强度。

summary_en.motivation: To compare the osseointegration strength of four porous metal implants in normal and osteoporotic rabbit bone.
summary_en.method: Implants were placed in femoral defects of ovariectomized and non-ovariectomized rabbits, and pull-out force was measured after 8 weeks.
summary_en.result: TANTALUM, TTM, and CONCELOC showed similar osseointegration strength, while ATLANT was significantly weaker.
summary_en.validation: In vivo animal study with biomechanical pull-out testing.
